bills.title: Taxpayer Funds Oversight and Accountability Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8340 directly implicates Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service and the Office of Management and Budget's payment integrity framework by imposing new oversight and reporting requirements on federal expenditures. Treasury faces implementation risk in adapting existing disbursement and reconciliation systems to meet any mandated accountability standards, as well as potential audit exposure if compliance timelines are aggressive.

bills.title: Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and Treasury Data Access Act
bills.nexus: H.R. 8463 directly implicates the Bureau of the Fiscal Service and potentially the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), as it governs Treasury's access to payment data systems for fraud detection before disbursements clear. The implementation risk centers on Treasury's operational capacity to stand up or modify pre-payment screening infrastructure while managing data-sharing authorities, privacy constraints, and interagency coordination without disrupting existing payment flows.

bills.title: Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agency Appropriations Act, 2027
bills.nexus: H.R. 8646 funds agencies including the Farm Service Agency and Rural Development programs, which administer loan, grant, and commodity support programs that interact with Treasury's debt collection and credit reform accounting rules under the Federal Credit Reform Act. Treasury's Fiscal Service bears implementation risk because disbursements, loan guarantees, and subsidy cost estimates must flow through federal credit accounts that Fiscal Service manages and audits.

bills.title: Making appropriations for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
bills.nexus: Treasury's nexus here is limited but real: the Office of Management and Budget and Treasury's fiscal operations (including the Bureau of the Fiscal Service) are affected whenever a major appropriations bill sets discretionary spending ceilings that drive cash-flow projections and debt-limit headroom calculations. If enacted, Treasury must coordinate apportionment timing and any borrowing adjustments needed to fund the authorized outlays for military construction and VA programs within the new fiscal year's budget authority.

bills.title: Taxpayer Experience Improvement Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7971 directly implicates IRS authorities under Treasury's jurisdiction, targeting taxpayer service operations, digital tools, and correspondence processes administered by the IRS's Taxpayer Services and IT modernization functions. Treasury must track implementation risk because the bill could impose new statutory mandates on IRS customer-facing systems at a time when the agency is already executing a multi-year modernization funded under the Inflation Reduction Act.

bills.title: IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7959 directly affects the IRS Whistleblower Office under Treasury's Internal Revenue Service, which administers award determinations and case coordination under IRC Section 7623. Proposed changes to award timelines, appeal rights, or eligibility criteria create implementation burden on IRS operations and expose Treasury to increased administrative litigation risk if procedural standards are tightened without adequate resourcing.

bills.title: Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act
bills.nexus: H.R. 8029 would require continued pay for military and civilian defense personnel during a government shutdown, directly implicating Treasury's role in executing appropriations and disbursing federal payroll through the Bureau of the Fiscal Service. Treasury must assess the legal and operational risk of disbursing funds absent a normal appropriation, as well as any Antideficiency Act exposure tied to payment authorization.

bills.title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Appropriations.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because DHS appropriations fund the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and Secret Service, both of which coordinate closely with Treasury on anti-money laundering enforcement and executive protection operations. Funding levels and any riders attached to the bill could affect Treasury's ability to execute joint investigative priorities and meet shared anti-illicit finance obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act.

bills.title: Disapproving the action of the District of Columbia Council in approving the D.C. Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025.
bills.nexus: Treasury's Office of Tax Policy monitors this resolution because congressional disapproval of D.C. tax law under the Home Rule Act can affect federal-D.C. tax base conformity and revenue coordination. Now that it is enacted law, Treasury and IRS must assess whether D.C. taxpayers face conflicting filing obligations or gaps in conformity with federal tax provisions that require administrative guidance.

bills.title: Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Appropriations.
bills.nexus: S. 3293 sets discretionary funding levels for the Department of Energy and the Army Corps of Engineers, but Treasury's interest stems from any tax credit direct-pay and transferability provisions tied to clean energy programs administered under IRA authorities, which fall within IRS and Office of Tax Policy purview. Treasury and IRS must monitor appropriations riders or reporting requirements that could constrain implementation of energy tax incentives or alter cash-flow timing for direct-pay claimants.

bills.title: Financial Services and General Government Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Appropriations.
bills.nexus: S. 3290 directly governs Treasury's annual discretionary funding levels, staffing, and operational authorities across bureaus including IRS, FinCEN, and the Office of Fiscal Service. Appropriations riders and spending caps in the bill can constrain IRS enforcement and modernization efforts, creating compliance revenue risk and implementation timeline exposure across ongoing technology investments.

bills.title: Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 137.
bills.nexus: S. 2572 funds the Department of Defense, but Treasury's interest lies in its appropriations provisions that may affect the Defense Finance and Accounting Service, interagency transfer authorities, or any debt-limit or general-provision riders that interact with Treasury's cash and debt management operations. Treasury's Office of Legislative Affairs and the Fiscal Assistant Secretary would monitor the bill for riders or rescissions that could constrain borrowing authority, disrupt intragovernmental fund flows, or impose reporting requirements on Treasury accounts.

bills.title: Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 140.
bills.nexus: S. 2587 does not directly appropriate funds to Treasury or invoke Treasury's statutory authorities, so Treasury's primary interest is indirect: any Labor or HHS funding levels affecting refundable tax credit administration (e.g., EITC, ACA premium tax credits) or workforce programs that interact with IRS compliance operations warrant monitoring. Treasury Legislative Affairs should track the bill for riders or report language that could constrain IRS appropriations flexibility or impose cross-agency mandates touching Tax Policy or IRS Service and Enforcement functions.

bills.title: Department of the Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 124.
bills.nexus: S. 2431 funds Interior and EPA programs but carries indirect Treasury equities because appropriations riders or rescissions can affect tax-expenditure-adjacent conservation programs (such as Land and Water Conservation Fund allocations) and environmental remediation liabilities that touch Superfund-related budget scoring. Treasury's Office of Legislative Affairs and the Office of Tax Policy would monitor any provisions altering conservation easement incentives or federal land transaction rules that interact with existing tax code authorities under IRC sections 170 and related provisions.

bills.title: Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 125.
bills.nexus: S. 2465 sets discretionary funding levels for THUD programs that flow through Treasury's cash management and debt-ceiling accounting functions, directly affecting the Office of Fiscal Service's disbursement obligations and borrowing headroom calculations. Treasury's Office of Legislative Affairs tracks it because any continuing resolution or rescission rider could alter spending timelines, creating reconciliation risk for Fiscal Service's appropriations warrant and IPAC settlement operations.

bills.title: Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 122.
bills.nexus: S. 2354 funds Commerce, Justice, Science, and related agencies for FY 2026, but Treasury's nexus is limited unless provisions touch Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), IRS, or Secret Service funding lines historically carried in related measures, or if riders affect Treasury-administered trade, sanctions, or forfeiture programs. Legislative Affairs should monitor floor amendments and report language for any provisions redirecting forfeiture fund receipts or imposing new reporting mandates on Treasury components that could trigger implementation or budget execution obligations.

bills.title: Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.status: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 112.
bills.nexus: S. 2256 sets discretionary funding levels for USDA and FDA programs, which directly affects Treasury's Office of Management and Budget liaison functions and any mandatory spending interactions scored against the federal budget baseline. Treasury's Fiscal Assistant Secretary and debt management operations must account for the appropriated outlays in cash flow projections and borrowing authority planning for FY 2026.

bills.title: Establishing the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2025 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2026 through 2034.
bills.status: Star Print ordered on the reported concurrent resolution.
bills.nexus: H.Con.Res. 14 sets aggregate revenue floors and debt-limit assumptions that directly constrain the Office of Tax Policy's legislative planning and the Office of Fiscal Assistant Secretary's debt management operations. Treasury monitors the resolution because its revenue and deficit targets shape the parameters within which tax legislation and borrowing authority will be negotiated over the ten-year window.

bills.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Internal Revenue Service relating to "Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales".
bills.nexus: H.J.Res. 25 directly nullifies an IRS rule issued under Treasury's tax administration authority, voiding the agency's effort to extend broker gross proceeds reporting requirements to digital asset transactions. The repeal eliminates an established compliance and revenue-reporting framework, requiring IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy to reassess how digital asset sales will be captured for tax enforcement purposes.
